subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Apple vs the FBI
description: A 60-second lesson on Apple vs the FBI.

hook.text: After a mass shooting in 2015, the FBI asked Apple to unlock an iPhone. Apple said no.

buildup.text: The FBI wanted Apple to build a special tool to bypass the phone's encryption and security features.

discovery.text: Apple argued that creating such a tool would endanger the security of every iPhone user worldwide.

twist.text: The FBI eventually unlocked the phone using a third-party hacking firm — without Apple's help.

climax.text: The case ended without a ruling, but the debate continues: should companies be forced to break their own security?

punchline.text: Build a master key. Everyone is at risk.

quiz.question: Why did Apple refuse to help the FBI unlock the iPhone?
options: Creating the tool would endanger security for all iPhone users
Apple didn't have the technical capability
The FBI didn't have a valid court order
